notes: RCON is the Quake III lineage protocol, NOT Source RCON: a single connectionless UDP datagram 0xFFFFFFFF + "rcon <password> <command>" sent to the game port, with the reply printed back as a print packet (SVC_RemoteCommand, sv_main.c). There is no enable switch and no separate RCON port - it answers on net_port (default PORT_SERVER 27960, qcommon.h) whenever the password cvar is non-empty; the engine registers it as Cvar_Get("rconPassword", "", CVAR_TEMP) in sv_init.c, but Quake III cvar lookup is case-insensitive and both the shipped and third-party etl_server.cfg write it as "set rconpassword", which is the spelling recorded here. Because it is CVAR_TEMP it must be set in the server cfg or on the command line. The engine rate-limits bad and repeated rcon packets (SVC_RateLimitAddress/SVC_RateLimit under sv_protect), and its own FIXME flags that big replies such as status overflow the 240-byte rcon redirection buffer across many out-of-band packets, so read the roster defensively. A dedicated etlded server also has a real stdin console; rcon is recorded here because it is the remote channel. COMMAND OWNERSHIP: the engine's SV_AddOperatorCommands registers status, serverinfo, systeminfo, say (dedicated servers only), cleartempbans, map, devmap, map_restart, killserver, heartbeat, dumpuser, fieldinfo, sectorlist, gameCompleteStatus and uptime; kick, clientkick and ban are NOT engine commands - they are game-module commands supplied by the bundled "legacy" mod (src/game/g_svcmds.c consoleCommandTable), and ET: Legacy explicitly removes the original ET engine's kick/banUser/banClient in SV_RemoveOperatorCommands. Running a different mod (etpub, silEnT, NoQuarter, etmain of another vintage) changes that half of the set; most competitive mods also add a shrubbot-style !kick/!ban layer that this file does not cover. TARGETING: kick, clientkick and ban all resolve their argument through G_ClientNumberFromString (g_cmds.c), a wrapper over G_ClientNumbersFromString that accepts a numeric client slot first (Q_isanumber, bounds-checked against level.maxclients and requiring the slot be CON_CONNECTED or CON_CONNECTING) and otherwise does a colour-stripped, lowercased SUBSTRING match on netnames, refusing unless exactly one player matches - so the slot number from column 1 of status is the only unambiguous id, which is what playerId is. MAX_CLIENTS is 64, so slots are 0-63. KICK SIDE EFFECT: usage is "kick <player name> [timeout]" and the timeout DEFAULTS TO 300, so a bare kick also temp-bans that address for 300 seconds (in-memory table of MAX_TEMPBAN_ADDRESSES = MAX_CLIENTS = 64 entries, cleared with cleartempbans); use "kick <slot> 0" for a kick with no temp ban and "kick all" to clear the server. Bots are kicked with timeout forced to 0. BAN: "ban <clientname>" only works on a currently connected client - G_PlayerBan reads that client's ip from userinfo and appends it to the g_banIPs IP-filter list (AddIPBan); it takes no reason and no duration, refuses bots, is an IP/mask ban rather than a GUID ban, and does NOT itself drop the client, so pair it with a kick. UNBAN: omitted on purpose - there is no unban-by-player command; the reverse operations are "removeip <ip-mask>" and "listip", which take an IP mask rather than a player id, plus cleartempbans for the engine temp-ban table. banList is likewise omitted: the persistent ban set lives in the g_banIPs cvar (space-separated masks, reloaded by G_ProcessIPBans), not in a ban file at a fixed path. MOTD: omitted - ET: Legacy has no motd command; the join-screen MOTD is the six cvars server_motd0..server_motd5, set from the server cfg. SAY: on a dedicated server say is the engine's SV_ConSay_f and is broadcast as chat prefixed with "console: "; "cp <message>" (centre print) and "qsay" are the other broadcast forms. STATUS OUTPUT: header is "num score ping name ... lastmsg address qport rate lastConnectTime" and each row is printf'd as %3i %5i then DEMO/CNCT/ZMBI or %4i, then the name left-padded, then lastmsg, address, qport, rate, lastConnectTime - note that current ET: Legacy has NO guid column (original ET 2.60b printed one), score can be negative, and the name column keeps its ^x colour codes, so strip them before display. DISAGREEMENT: hosting knowledge bases written for original Wolf:ET (e.g. legionhosting) list banClient, unban and banlist as rcon commands; grepping both the engine command table and the legacy mod consoleCommandTable shows ET: Legacy registers none of them, and only the kick/clientkick/ban/status/say/cp overlap is trustworthy. ET: Legacy is a standalone free client, not a Steam app, hence appId null; it is normally installed alongside Wolfenstein: Enemy Territory 2.60b assets.
